evidence.note: R-perf-landscape (THEORETICAL) and R-perf-inventory (CONFIRMED) already filed the landscape/inventory this builds on; grep shows testtimes.rollup already exposes per_file/skew/critical_path_floor_s and flakyrate.proposals already does quarantine, but there is no ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py and no prop_split_share/prop_shard_skew/prop_select_miss_min/prop_select_min_runs knob (refutation would be finding either).

ddflow brief: conformance r-reuse-core (reuse testtimes + flakyrate), r-small-files, r-everything-configurable (every threshold a [perf_metrics] knob), r-tell-dont-discover (next_call names the decision), D-no-duckdb, D-sched-no-daemon.
Committed 2182ab8cc: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py (propose_split_files, propose_shard_or_workers, propose_selection) + tests/test_perf_prop_tests.py + 4 [perf_metrics] knobs.

chunk_findings.detail: Given `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": None, "per_file": {"slow_test.py": 80}}` the `or 0.0` coercion makes `floor <= 0` and the function returns `[]`. A missing floor is an unavailable probe, not a measured zero, so the caller treats “nothing to split” as a pass. The same pattern is in `propose_shard_or_workers`: a rollup with `critical_path_floor_s=100`, `per_file={"a.py": 90}` and no `skew` key becomes `skew=0.0`, which is below `prop_shard_skew`, so the result is a `workers` proposal whose `because` says the suite is not skewed when skew was never measured.
chunk_findings.title: propose_split_files

chunk_findings.detail: The size rule is not applied unless the caller passes `max_file_bytes > 0`. The default is `0`, and that branch skips the size check. Input `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10, "per_file": {"tiny.py": 9}}`, `sizes={"tiny.py": 100}`, `max_file_bytes` omitted yields a `split_file` proposal for a 100-byte file. The stated rule is share above the knob and over the size rule; duration alone must not split.
chunk_findings.title: propose_split_files

chunk_findings.detail: Every kind returns the same string, `propose only: record the change ddflow decision add`. A `split_file` proposal does not name the SZ split command that is supposed to accept it, and shard, worker, and selection proposals likewise do not name the call that performs that change. Required fields are also absent: sample size, effect size, expected seconds saved per run and per day, and risk are not on `Proposal` and are not filled by any generator.
chunk_findings.title: Proposal.next_call

chunk_findings.detail: Missing or non-numeric misses are not recorded as unavailable. `{"misses": None}` (and a missing key) becomes `0` via `or 0`, so ten runs with no miss field and `selected_fraction` present return `None`, i.e. “selection is safe”, when the probe did not run. `{"misses": "unavailable"}` hits `int("unavailable")` and raises `ValueError` instead of an unavailable result. Narrowing is also unimplemented: runs with `misses=0` and `selected_fraction=1.0` across `prop_select_min_runs` never produce a narrow proposal.
chunk_findings.title: propose_selection

chunk_findings.detail: `test_an_unskewed_suite_proposes_a_worker_raise_not_a_shard` and `test_a_skewed_suite_is_a_shard_of_the_slowest_file` both build rollups whose own `skew` is 1.0. For 30/30/40 at 8 workers, `_rollup` sets `critical_path_floor_s = max(40, 100/8) = 40` and `skew = 40/40 = 1.0`; for 90/5/5 it is `90/90 = 1.0`. Both are `>= prop_shard_skew` (0.9). Raising workers cannot beat the 40s file, so the “unskewed” fixture is the shard case, not a worker raise. The two tests demand opposite kinds for the same skew signal, so one assertion is wrong for any implementation that shards when `skew` exceeds the knob.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_prop_tests.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_small_share_is_not_a_split_candidate` does not construct a small critical-path share. With durations 1.0 and 1.0 and `workers=8`, `_rollup` sets `critical_path_floor_s = max(1.0, 2/8) = 1.0`, so `tests/test_a.py` is the entire floor (share 1.0 > `prop_split_share` 0.5) and its size 500 exceeds `max_file_bytes` 100. A splitter that follows “share of the critical path exceeds X and over the size rule” must emit a split; the test expects `[]`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_prop_tests.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The size rule is still not the `[quality].max_file_bytes` limit unless the caller passes `max_file_bytes > 0`. The default remains `0`, and `size <= max_file_bytes` then only rejects a missing or non-positive size. Given `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10, "per_file": {"tiny.py": 9}}`, `sizes={"tiny.py": 100}`, and `max_file_bytes` omitted, `100 <= 0` is false, so the function emits a `split_file` proposal for a 100-byte file. Duration plus any recorded size must not split when the size rule was never supplied.
chunk_findings.title: propose_split_files

chunk_findings.detail: A run that never recorded misses is still treated as a measured zero on the narrow path, and a missing probe is still indistinguishable from “no proposal”. `_count_misses` skips a missing or non-numeric `misses` and leaves `total` at 0; it does not mark the series unavailable. Input `[{"selected_fraction": 1.0}] * prop_select_min_runs` (no `misses` key, or `"misses": "unavailable"`) therefore fails the widen check and hits `all(_fraction(r) == 1.0)`, which returns a `narrow` proposal whose evidence hardcodes `"misses": 0`. That is a probe that did not run recorded as zero misses and a safe narrowing, which the function’s own comment says must not force a NARROW. The same ten runs with a fraction other than 1.0 still return `None`, so “selection is safe / nothing to do” and “misses were never measured” stay the same result.
chunk_findings.title: propose_selection

chunk_findings.detail: The widening logic in `propose_selection` checks `misses >= cfg.prop_select_miss_min`, but the knob name retrieved via `_section_knobs` is `prop_select_miss_min`, whereas the docstring mentions `prop_select_miss_min`. However, `PerfMetricsConfig` in the config section defines it with a different default or attribute name if mismatch occurs (e.g. `prop_select_miss_min` vs `prop_select_miss_min`), causing potential AttributeError if the config field is accessed. Given input runs with enough misses, `cfg.prop_select_miss_min` is read, but if `PerfMetricsConfig` defines it as `prop_select_miss_min` and `prop_select_miss_min` is not defined on the config object, it raises an `AttributeError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: Narrowing does not require zero measured misses, and the evidence lies about it. After the widen check fails, `if measured and all(_fraction(r) == 1.0 for r in runs)` still returns a `narrow` proposal and hardcodes `evidence["misses"]` to 0. With `cfg.prop_select_miss_min=2` and `runs=[{"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 1}, {"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 1}]`, `_count_misses` returns `(2, True)`, `2 >= 2` is false only if the knob is higher — for miss_min 3, or for miss_min 2 with a single counted miss of 1 across two full-selection runs, widen is skipped and the function still emits `narrow` with `misses: 0`. That proposes tightening selection after a periodic full run already found a miss the selection would not have run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:propose_selection

chunk_findings.detail: A non-finite critical-path floor is treated as a real measurement. `_floor` only rejects non-numbers and `<= 0`, so `float("nan")` is returned (`nan <= 0` is false). In `propose_split_files`, `secs / floor` is NaN and `nan < share` is false, so the share gate never drops the file: `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": float("nan"), "per_file": {"big.py": 1.0}}`, `sizes={"big.py": 1000}`, `max_file_bytes=100` emits a `split_file` proposal. In `propose_shard_or_workers`, a NaN `skew` fails `skew >= prop_shard_skew` and falls through to a `workers` raise. A probe that did not produce a finite floor is supposed to be unavailable, not a split or a worker increase.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:_floor

chunk_findings.detail: A non-finite `skew` is still treated as “not skewed”, so the worker-raise branch fires. `_floor` now rejects NaN/Inf, but `skew = float(rollup.get("skew"))` accepts any `int`/`float` (including `bool`, since `bool` is an `int`) and the only gate is `skew >= cfg.prop_shard_skew`. `nan >= threshold` is false, so `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "per_file": {"a.py": 1.0}, "skew": float("nan")}` returns a `workers` proposal whose evidence claims the suite is not skewed. `skew=True` becomes `1.0` and can emit `shard` the same way. Unavailable skew must stay `None`, not a raise or a shard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:propose_shard_or_workers

chunk_findings.detail: Per-file seconds are not checked for finiteness, so a garbage duration still clears the share gate. `nan < share` and `inf < share` are both false, so the file is not dropped. `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "per_file": {"big.py": float("nan")}}`, `sizes={"big.py": 1000}`, `max_file_bytes=100` emits `split_file` with NaN `serial_s` and `share_of_floor`. Same for `float("inf")`. A non-finite sample is unavailable, not a split candidate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:propose_split_files

chunk_findings.detail: Miss counts are coerced with `int(m)` without a finite, non-negative check. `int(float("nan"))` and `int(float("inf"))` raise `ValueError`, so one bad run aborts proposal generation instead of being recorded unavailable. A negative count is added as a real measurement and can cancel real misses: `runs=[{"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 5}, {"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": -5}]` with `prop_select_min_runs=2` and `prop_select_miss_min=3` yields `(0, True)` and a `narrow` proposal whose evidence hardcodes `misses: 0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:_count_misses

chunk_findings.detail: `_workers` only accepts a strict `int`, so a JSON-style float worker count is treated as 1 and the saving collapses to a measured zero. `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "workers": 4.0, "per_file": {"big.py": 8.0}}` with `sizes={"big.py": 1000}` and `max_file_bytes=100` makes `propose_split_files` emit `expected_saving_s_run=0.0` (`8 - 8/1`) instead of `6.0`. The same default is used for the shard saving. A missing or non-int count is unavailable, and `Proposal` says an unknown figure is `None`, never zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:_workers

chunk_findings.detail: Per-file durations are not validated before `max` or the saving arithmetic, and the non-finite check misses `-inf` and non-numbers. `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "skew": 0.9, "per_file": {"a.py": "x", "b.py": 1.0}}` raises `TypeError` in `max` instead of returning `None`. `per_file={"a.py": float("-inf")}` with the same floor and skew returns a `shard` proposal whose `expected_saving_s_run` is NaN. `per_file={"a.py": True}` is accepted as a 1-second sample and sharded. A duration that was not measured is unavailable, not a shard candidate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:propose_shard_or_workers

chunk_findings.detail: A finite non-negative float miss count is truncated with `int`, so a fractional miss becomes a measured zero and can authorize a narrow. `runs=[{"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 0.9}, {"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 0.9}]` with `prop_select_min_runs=2` and `prop_select_miss_min=1` yields `(0, True)` and a `narrow` proposal whose evidence claims no misses, even though each run recorded a miss. Narrowing on a truncated zero is the unsafe direction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:_count_misses

Given `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "skew": 0.9, "per_file": {"a.py": "x"}}`, `max` raises a `TypeError` when comparing a string to itself or during key evaluation, which crashes the proposal generator instead of safely returning `None` or skipping invalid entries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier missing-count objection still stands. `_workers` still turns a missing, non-numeric, or non-positive `workers` into `1`, and both `propose_split_files` and `propose_shard_or_workers` then publish that as a measured saving. `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "per_file": {"big.py": 8.0}}` with `sizes={"big.py": 1000}` and `max_file_bytes=100` yields `expected_saving_s_run=0.0` (`8 - 8/1`) instead of `None`. `Proposal` says an unknown figure is unavailable, never zero. Guarding `4.0` so `int(4.0)` is 4 does not fix this path; a float that is finite is still truncated, not rejected.

chunk_findings.detail: Per-file durations are still not validated before `max`, and the check after it still misses `-inf`, non-numbers, and bools. `rollup={"critical_path_floor_s": 10.0, "skew": 0.9, "per_file": {"a.py": "x", "b.py": 1.0}}` raises `TypeError` in `max`. `per_file={"a.py": float("-inf")}` with the same floor and skew passes `slowest_s != slowest_s or slowest_s == float("inf")` and returns a `shard` proposal whose `expected_saving_s_run` is NaN. `per_file={"a.py": True}` is still accepted as a 1-second sample. The same input plus `"skew": 0.9` makes the shard proposal report `expected_saving_s_run=0.0` while `evidence["workers"]` is absent. The triage probe never touches this default.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:_workers

chunk_findings.detail: A finite non-negative float miss count is still truncated with `int`, so a fractional miss becomes a measured zero and can authorize a narrow. `runs=[{"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 0.9}, {"selected_fraction": 1.0, "misses": 0.9}]` with `prop_select_min_runs=2` and `prop_select_miss_min=1` yields `(0, True)` and a `narrow` proposal whose evidence claims no misses. Narrowing on a truncated zero is the unsafe direction. Finite `0.9` is not rejected by the non-finite filter the triage cites, and this function still has no “fractional miss is unavailable” guard.

chunk_findings.detail: `propose_shard_or_workers` never compares the slowest file to the critical-path floor, which is the skew rule its own docstring states. It branches on an opaque `rollup["skew"]` and then writes that number as if it were the file’s share of the floor. Given `critical_path_floor_s=100`, `per_file={"slow.py": 10, "other.py": 9}`, `skew=0.99`, `workers=4` and `prop_shard_skew=0.5`, it emits a shard of `slow.py` whose `because` says `slow.py` “is 0.99 of the floor” (it is 0.10). The inverse input, slowest share 0.99 and `skew=0.10`, skips the shard and proposes raising workers, which cannot lower a floor already equal to one file. Wall clock over `serial_seconds` is stored in evidence and never used for the decision.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:176

chunk_findings.detail: `_count_misses` accepts a float miss count and then `int()`-truncates it toward zero, so a positive miss can become a measured zero. Given `prop_select_min_runs` runs each `{"misses": 0.9, "selected_fraction": 1.0}`, the total becomes 0 with `measured=True`, the widen check fails, and `propose_selection` returns a narrow proposal. That is the unsafe direction: the risk text itself says one missed failure is a silent regression, and these runs did record misses.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:264

chunk_findings.detail: `Proposal.next_call` ignores `advice` and always returns a template with `<item>`, so the named accept command is not the exact call for that proposal. A split proposal whose advice file is `tests/test_slow.py` still tells the caller to run `ddflow split <item>` / `ddflow_task action=split id=<item>`, which does not name the file the evidence selected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/prop_tests.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: Given `per_file` durations 4s, 3s and 3s with `workers=1`, wall clock equals the serial sum (10s) and the slowest file's share is 0.4, below `prop_shard_skew=0.5`. The stated rule only changes the xdist worker count when wall clock over serial-equivalent shows skew, and only shards on historical duration skew. This input has neither signal, so `propose_shard_or_workers` must return nothing. The test requires `kind == "workers"` and `advice["kind"] == "raise"`, which locks in a false worker-count proposal.
